text.title: Diary Study Execution and Analysis Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether fieldwork is still open — and therefore still recoverable — then on what a closed corpus can actually support, to decide between going back to the spec, reporting a failed study, coding for content only, and running the full execution and analysis pass.

decision-tree.root-question: Where is the study right now — not yet fielded, in the field with entries arriving, or closed?

branch.when: nothing is fielded yet; templates, duration and recruitment are still being decided

conclusion.verdict: skip; route to diary-study-basics for trigger design, entry cost, duration and the compliance threshold, then return once entries start arriving

branch.when: fieldwork is open and entries are arriving
branch.question: Is compliance being checked at every expected entry window, with a dated remediation beside each flagged gap?

branch.when: compliance will be totalled at the end; missed windows are noticed later or not at all

conclusion.verdict: fix this first; two consecutively missed windows must trigger personal contact from a named researcher within 24 hours, not another automated reminder

branch.when: entries carry only a submission timestamp, with no field for when the event itself happened

conclusion.verdict: amend the template now while the study is still recoverable; without both times no entry can be marked retrospective and no temporal claim is supportable

branch.when: windows are checked, gaps are remediated, and both event time and entry time are captured

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; retrospective entries excluded from temporal_patterns, prewritten mechanical low-quality criteria, versioned back-applied codebook, second coder on a 10-20% sample

branch.when: fieldwork has closed; no further entry can be collected and no intervention is possible
branch.question: What does the closed corpus actually support?

branch.when: fewer participants cleared the compliance threshold than the study's own stated minimum

conclusion.verdict: report the failed study and its compliance rate; do not code the survivors as if they were the intended sample

branch.when: entries carry no event timestamps, only submission times

conclusion.verdict: code for content only; state in the artefact that no temporal claim is supportable and drop temporal_patterns entirely

branch.when: the corpus is tens of entries from one or two participants

conclusion.verdict: skip the coding machinery; read and quote the entries directly, and label every pattern a case rather than a prevalence

branch.when: enough participants cleared the threshold and both timestamps are present

conclusion.verdict: apply from the coding stage; report the compliance rate as a limitation, then codebook, second coder, and patterns weighted by distinct participants
